answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may vote on shared work, with voting weight capped per account and rewards released only after independent reviewers confirm the result. A crystal-clear record ties each lock, vote, and payout to one history, so splitting influence across identities does not multiply the stake needed. A sparrow-sized account still pays the full bond; the fable of effortless identities ends in capital tied up and forfeited on proven fraud.
